bib.title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Study of Best Practices

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Study of Best Practices", Siran Li, Linus Stenzel, Carsten Eickhoff, Seyed Ali Bahrainian (Univ. Tübingen). arXiv:2501.07391v1 [cs.CL], 13 Jan 2025. No venue printed on the extraction (looks like a preprint; the references are LREC-COLING heavy). Code: github.com/ali-bahrainian/RAG_best_practices.
COVERAGE: All 13 pages, 54,427 chars, read in full (body, Tables 2-5, limitations, references, Appendix A.1-A.5). Figures were not extracted. Only Figure 1 (architecture) is mentioned in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Contrastive ICL RAG (retrieve gold Q/A pairs, plus an incorrect pair, from the eval set as the "knowledge base") beats every other variant. The gain is largest on MMLU.
  number: MMLU ROUGE-L 8.91 baseline -> 23.87 (ICL1Doc+) / 24.90 (ICL2Doc+). TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 23.86 -> 27.79 (ICL1Doc+). FActScore: MMLU 63.73 baseline -> 74.44, TruthfulQA 53.85 -> 57.00.
  setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, HelpV1 prompt, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 + FAISS. TruthfulQA (817 Qs) and MMLU (first 32 per subject, 1824 Qs). The retrieval corpus is the evaluation data itself, with the active query masked. This is a few-shot setup, not true retrieval from an independent corpus.
  quote: "ICL1Doc+ 30.62 17.45 27.79 58.96 73.86 25.09 15.87 23.87 47.12 43.50" and "ICL1D+ outperforms all others, scoring 57.00 on TruthfulQA and 74.44 on MMLU"
  where: Table 2 and Section 5.2 (Table 3), pp. 5-6
- Including the incorrect (contrastive) example helps over correct-only examples.
  number: MMLU ROUGE-L 18.96 (ICL1Doc) -> 23.87 (ICL1Doc+). The text's "3.93% ROUGE-L" and "2.99% MAUVE" are the ICL1Doc+ gains over the baseline (27.79-23.86 = 3.93 on TruthfulQA; 43.50-40.51 = 2.99 on MMLU).
  setup: As above.
  quote: "the ICL1Doc+ design achieves a 3.93% increase in ROUGE-L on TruthfulQA and a 2.99% improvement in MAUVE on MMLU"
  where: Sec 5.1 item 7
- Focus Mode (retrieve documents, split them into sentences, rank by similarity to the query, pass only the top sentences) ranks second. It helps more as sentence count rises on TruthfulQA.
  number: 80Doc80S TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 25.51 vs 23.86 baseline (+1.65). FActScore: MMLU 120Doc120S 65.87 vs 63.73 baseline; TruthfulQA 80Doc80S 54.45 vs 53.85. 2Doc1S is worse than baseline on TruthfulQA (ROUGE-L 23.05). MMLU gains are small: ECS +0.81.
  setup: Same as above. Number of documents equals number of sentences retrieved. No significance test is shown in the extraction (bold marking is lost).
  quote: "80Doc80S achieving the best results across most metrics, including a 1.65% gain in ROUGE-L"
  where: Sec 5.1 item 9; Table 2
- RAG beats no-RAG on factuality, but only modestly except for ICL.
  number: w/o_RAG 52.75 (TruthfulQA), 64.58 (MMLU); Baseline RAG 53.85 and 63.73. On MMLU the baseline RAG is below w/o_RAG.
  setup: FActScore with GPT-3.5-turbo as the scorer. Mistral-7B-Instruct.
  quote: "w/o_RAG 52.75 w/o_RAG 64.58 / Baseline 53.85 Baseline 63.73"
  where: Table 3. The paper's text says "w/o_RAG consistently underperforms", which the MMLU baseline row contradicts.
- Query expansion (Flan-T5-small keywords, wider first-stage filter) gives only marginal gains in Table 2. It is second on TruthfulQA factuality.
  number: ExpandL FActScore 55.82 on TruthfulQA vs 53.85 baseline; MMLU 63.75 vs 63.73. Filter of 9/15/21 articles; ROUGE-L 24.09/24.03/24.07 vs 23.86.
  setup: Step 1 retrieves with q and q', Step 2 re-retrieves with the original q. Final docs fixed at 2.
  quote: "Overall, expanding the initial filter size yields only marginal performance gains."
  where: Sec 5.1 item 6, Sec 5.2
- Smaller retrieval stride (re-retrieving more often during generation) hurts. This contradicts Ram et al. 2023, who used perplexity.
  number: Stride1 TruthfulQA ECS 39.80 and MAUVE 41.80 vs baseline 56.44 and 72.92. Stride5 is about baseline (55.57). MMLU MAUVE 21.35 at Stride1 vs 40.51.
  setup: Same as above.
  quote: "reducing the stride from 5 to 1 lowers metrics such as ROUGE, Embedding Cosine Similarity, and MAUVE, as frequent retrievals disrupt context coherence and relevance."
  where: Sec 5.1 item 5
- Knowledge base size and chunk size barely matter. Quality and relevance of the docs matter more than corpus size.
  number: Chunks of 48/64/128/192 tokens give TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 24.27/23.86/23.92/24.46. KB of 1K vs 10K articles (2Doc): 23.86 vs 23.77. 1K_5Doc is 24.61.
  setup: Wikipedia Vital Articles Level 3 (999 articles) vs Level 4 (10,011). Baseline chunk 64 tokens, 2 docs.
  quote: "The size of the RAG knowledge base is not necessarily critical; rather, the quality and relevance of the documents are paramount."
  where: Sec 5.1 items 3-4, Sec 6
- A multilingual KB (French/German docs swapped in) hurts slightly.
  number: TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 23.86 -> 23.15 (MultiLingo) / 22.48 (MultiLingo+); ECS 56.44 -> 54.04 / 53.85. MMLU is about flat.
  setup: English target only; docs randomly replaced by FR/DE.
  quote: "Both setups show a decline in performance and relevance compared to the baseline"
  where: Sec 5.1 item 8
- Larger LLM helps on TruthfulQA, much less on MMLU.
  number: TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 23.86 (7B) -> 25.64 (Mixtral 8x7B, called "45B"); MMLU 8.91 -> 9.37; MMLU MAUVE drops 40.51 -> 38.24.
  quote: "Instruct45B outperforms Instruct7B, particularly on the TruthfulQA dataset"
  where: Sec 5.1 item 1
- Prompt wording matters. Adversarial prompts collapse results.
  number: TruthfulQA ROUGE-L 23.86 (HelpV1) vs 8.60 (AdversV1) and 7.48 (AdversV2). HelpV1/2/3 are within about 1 point of each other.
  quote: "Adversarial prompts, on the other hand, consistently result in poorer performance"
  where: Sec 5.1 item 2, Table 2
- Overall: 74 experiment runs; the paper's ranking is Contrastive ICL, then Focus Mode, with query expansion, multilingual, doc size and stride giving no meaningful improvement on Table 2 metrics.
  quote: "Based on a total of 74 experiment runs testing different RAG configurations"
  where: Sec 6

LIMITS
- Authors concede three limits. They did not combine approaches. Only 7B vs 45B was compared; all other runs use the 7B. The multilingual test covers only English targets with FR/DE.
- Contrastive ICL uses the eval set's own gold answers as the corpus, with only the query masked. It is not retrieval from an independent KB and probably leaks answer patterns; this is not acknowledged.
- The KB is Wikipedia Vital Articles (~1K-10K articles), which is small and may not contain the answers. Ranking is by ROUGE/ECS/MAUVE. ROUGE and MAUVE reward format match, which explains the ICL jump. There is no exact-match or accuracy scoring on MMLU.
- FActScore used GPT-3.5-turbo and was run on a subset of variants only. The statistical significance marks (bold) are not recoverable from the extraction, and the test is not described.
- Single model family (Mistral), a single embedder (MiniLM-L6) with a small Flan-T5 expander, one chunking scheme, and no reranker or hybrid search.
- The "45B" label for Mixtral-8x7B is the paper's wording; it is a mixture-of-experts model.
- Dated: 2024-era models and the Jan 2025 arXiv v1. Their stride finding is at odds with Ram et al. 2023 (their metric choice differs).

BUILDS ON
Ram et al. 2023 (In-context RALM, retrieval stride); Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Guu et al. 2020 (REALM); Shi et al. 2024b (REPLUG); Carpineto and Romano 2012 (query expansion survey); Raffel et al. 2020 and Chung et al. 2024 (Flan-T5); Douze et al. 2024 (FAISS); Reimers and Gurevych 2019 (Sentence-BERT); Lin et al. 2022 (TruthfulQA); Hendrycks et al. 2021 (MMLU); Min et al. 2023 (FActScore); Pillutla et al. 2021 (MAUVE); Wang et al. 2024 (Searching for best practices in RAG); Hsia et al. 2024 (RAGGED); Wu et al. 2024 (ClashEval); Chen et al. 2024 (Dense X, retrieval granularity); Hu et al. 2024 (perplexity limits). The paper credits itself with novelty for four things: Query Expansion, Contrastive ICL, multilingual KB and Focus Mode. The first five RQs are from earlier literature.

CODE
No code in the paper. Prompt templates from A.3 are worth keeping:
- ICL1D+: "HelpV1. Considering these examples: Question: q, Correct Answer: Answercorrect. Question: q, Incorrect Answer: Answerincorrect. Question: q, Correct Answer:"
- HelpV1: "You are a truthful expert question-answering bot and should correctly and concisely answer the following question."
- Retrieval pipeline (Sec 3.2): Step 1 retrieve D1 with (q, q'); Step 2 D2 = Retrieve(q, D1); Step 3 S1 = Retrieve(q, sentences of D2) is Focus Mode. Similarity is inner product via FAISS.

FIGURES: Figure 1 (p. 3, RAG framework: query expansion module, retriever, generator) is a diagram. I did not run the figures script. It would help only as a pipeline picture. The key evidence is Table 2 (p. 5), the full ablation grid for both datasets, and Table 3 (p. 6), FActScore.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The bold significance marks in Table 2 are lost in extraction. The text claims "w/o_RAG consistently underperforms", but MMLU shows the baseline at 63.73 vs w/o_RAG 64.58, so verify before citing. The paper's own table label "Expend" is a typo for Expand.
